cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T2 slows T1's plan; T4 answers T3; T6 rebuts T5; T10 turns T9's note into a control record.
cells.limitation: T5 pivots to motive with no link to T4's pair-testing plan, which nobody takes up.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T7 splits the advice by motive (keep routine vs fear); T8 and T9 build on that split.
cells.limitation: T3's non-product causes (detergent, shower, wind) are never developed after T4 folds them into controls.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: Test-versus-drop (T2, T11) and product-versus-other-cause (T3, T4) are examined.
cells.limitation: No turn considers what the three products contain (acids, retinoids, fragrance) as the first clue.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T4 narrows its plan to include pairs after T3; T11 accepts T10's patch tests while still disagreeing.
cells.limitation: Skeptic's alternative causes are absorbed as held-constant variables (T4) rather than reshaping the plan.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D sharpens to calm first, newest product a suspect not a verdict, retest-or-drop disputed.
cells.limitation: T11's closing disagreement names no fact that would settle retest versus drop.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T2 restates T1's reintroduction plan accurately before objecting to its timing.
cells.limitation: T3 says both assume a product is guilty, though T2 only removed a possible irritant.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T3 names the guilty-product assumption and joint effects; T4 answers that single tests miss interactions.
cells.limitation: T10's forearm-equals-face assumption and T11's cost-of-wrong claim go unchallenged.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T8's red flags and T9's irritation-more-common-than-allergy claim are sound general guidance.
cells.limitation: T10 calls forearm testing a far cleaner signal and a day or two enough; suspected overstatement.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T2 flags timing as its own addition to Taleb; T5 frames the money motive with perhaps.
cells.limitation: T10 states forearm testing as far cleaner without hedging despite facial skin differing.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T4: you've landed a real hit, then narrows to pairs and admits joint causes are hardest.
cells.limitation: The Subtractor never answers T6's point that nothing mentions money; T11 accepts patch tests without stated cause.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: T5-T6 ask whether the user wants to save the routine or rule out something serious.
cells.limitation: T5 leans toward reframing the request as keep-or-drop before T6 restores the worry reading.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: Three products started together drives T1's isolation and T4's pair testing.
cells.limitation: Few user details exist; product types, routine and skin history are never drawn in.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E keeps the user's goal: if you want to keep your routine, then reintroduce.
cells.limitation: T11 pushes the Subtractor's preference to skip identification, the user's stated aim.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T8 separates urgent symptoms from a mild sting that fades after rinsing.
cells.limitation: T5 invents a purchase-cost motive; no timeframe given for how long calm-down takes.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on severity, fading after rinsing, wanting to keep the routine.
cells.limitation: What else changed (Section A) is logged in T9 but no branch says what it implies; product types never asked.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T5 and T6 offer save-the-routine versus worry; Section D asks which, only you can say.
cells.limitation: T5 phrases the culprit-not-clean-break motive close to a conclusion before T6 checks it.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3: the newest thing is just the easiest suspect; tidy is not the same as true.
cells.limitation: The belief that stinging signals harm, rather than expected adjustment, is never surfaced.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T11 weighs the cost of being wrong against the value of knowing.
cells.limitation: The knowing-versus-simplicity conflict stays the speakers'; only Section D ties it to the user.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T6 names plain worry about allergy or damage; T9 notes panic has a cost too.
cells.limitation: T9's panic label sits a little dismissively beside T6's legitimate worry.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section D: either could be true, and only you can say.
cells.limitation: Only one reflective question is offered; T11's retest-or-drop is not posed to the user.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Section E lays out urgent care, subtract, reintroduce, drop, dermatologist patch testing.
cells.limitation: Keeping one valued product while pausing the other two is never considered.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T2 costs reintroduction as re-irritation; T11 costs dropping as never knowing.
cells.limitation: Time and repeated flare cost of T4's singles-then-pairs schedule is not stated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: swelling, blisters, spreading rash favour urgent care; fading after rinsing favours subtracting.
cells.limitation: No observable sign defines when skin is calm; T10 and E use ungrounded day counts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T9 separates common irritation from allergy; T4 flags joint causes as hardest.
cells.limitation: T3's non-product causes are never ranked against product causes as more or less likely.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: T9's written log and T10's dermatologist patch testing fit a mild-to-unclear reaction.
cells.limitation: Pair testing (Section E) adds a long schedule for a mild sting without weighing it.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T8 lists symptoms in plain words; T9's write today what you used is concrete.
cells.limitation: Joint causes in T4 and control record in T10 are mildly technical.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T6 that reading = T5; T10 that note = T9; T11 accept patch tests = T10.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Eleven turns, all within word range per deterministic checks.
cells.limitation: Section E runs as one dense paragraph of five branches.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Tester plans, Subtractor removes, Skeptic doubts the story; T4 announces its narrowed plan.
cells.limitation: All three minds share one plain register and near-identical turn lengths across T1-T11.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns rarely repeat; Section E's red-flag list reuses T8 for a clear purpose.
cells.limitation: Section E restates T8's red flags nearly verbatim.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T8: waiting around is a bad plan when the skin is burning.
cells.limitation: Tension stays moderate; the stakes of a wrong retest are never made concrete.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T4 narrows to pair testing because T3 showed interactions escape single tests.
cells.limitation: T11 accepts patch tests without naming what in T10 changed its view.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T3: the mind loves a tidy culprit; T8: a different animal.
cells.limitation: Voices are courteous and similar; little individual temperament beyond the stated lens.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T3: tidy is not the same as true; T6: rescuing a shelf of bottles.
cells.limitation: Few analogies or vivid examples after T6; T10 and T11 are procedural.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T8's red flags then T9's panic has a cost give one shift in tone.
cells.limitation: Uniform turn lengths and steady intensity from T1 to T11; the ending is quiet.

strengths: T7 splits the advice by the user's motive, and Section D returns that as a question only the user can answer.
T4 concedes T3's interaction point and narrows its testing plan to include pairs.
Section E gives observable branches: red flags to urgent care, fading sting to subtraction.
weaknesses: No mind (T1-T11) considers the products' ingredients or types as the most direct clue.
T10 claims forearm patch testing gives a far cleaner signal over a day or two, unchallenged.
All three minds share one register and near-identical turn lengths, flattening voice and rhythm.

symptoms.observed: Ingredient contents of the three products never considered as a clue to the cause.
symptoms.evidence: Stop all three, let the skin settle, then add them back

symptoms.observed: Forearm patch test claimed cleaner than face and sufficient in a day or two.
symptoms.evidence: That gives a far cleaner signal than the face.

symptoms.observed: Other changes that week logged but no branch on what finding one would imply.
symptoms.evidence: how bad it felt, and what else changed

symptoms.observed: Test durations are generic counts; no observable sign defines when skin is calm.
symptoms.evidence: on a small spot, like the inner forearm, for a day or two

symptoms.observed: Three minds share one plain register and near-identical turn lengths.
symptoms.evidence: The one that brings back the sting is your answer.

findings.description: Forearm patch test over a day or two called a far cleaner signal; facial skin is more reactive and allergic reactions can appear later.
Attributions to Mill, Taleb and Kahneman are plausible paraphrases with no source evidence attached.
